blocks.x: Zero-trust for OSS/BSS under DORA timelines — critical-third-party register complete and resilience testing moved from annual to continuous
a telecom infrastructure group facing DORA deadlines with an ICT estate assembled from twenty years of procurement. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline gap analysis read like a to-do list: critical third parties cataloged in a spreadsheet last touched at signing, resilience testing annual and theatrical, and incident reporting paths that had never carried a real incident.
DORA's language was precise; the estate's reality was not. Every requirement traded against an operational constraint someone had learned to live with.

We ran DORA as gates, not a binder: the critical-third-party register built as living data with contract clauses mapped to evidence, resilience testing moved to continuous scenario execution against real runbooks, incident reporting rehearsed with the actual on-call chain, and the evidence register the supervisor walks maintained by the same system that produces the tests. The binder became a by-product.
